slides.texte_overlay:
Small habits that make people
respect you instantly
Answer messages within a day. Even if it's "Got it, I'll get back to you Friday." People respect the guy who never leaves them hanging, and it's the easiest reputation to build.
Show up prepared. Read the email before the meeting, know the names before the dinner. Being prepared tells people you take them seriously, so they take you seriously back.
Admit mistakes fast. "That was on me, here's how I'll fix it." Owning it before anyone points it out earns more respect than pretending you never get anything wrong.
Keep learning every day. Five minutes of history, art or science. People quietly respect someone who always seems to know a bit more than they expected.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. People quietly respect someone who always seems to know a bit more than they expected.

slides.texte_overlay: Treat everyone the same. The CEO and the cleaner get the same hello, the same eye contact, the same thank you. People notice, and it's one of the strongest signs of real character.
Don't complain in public. Bad boss, bad day, bad weather. Keep it for your close friends. The guy who stays positive when everyone else is moaning is the one people look up to.
Keep your space and your look tidy. Clean shoes, a made bed, a clear desk. It's small, but people read it as "this guy has his life together," and that earns respect without a word.
